description: A list's distinct items follow pushes and shifts in first-occurrence order
code:
visits = ["lab", "den", "lab", "hall"]
rooms = visits.distinct()
visits.push("den")
visits.push("attic")
assert(rooms, ["lab", "den", "hall", "attic"])
visits.shift()
rooms

description: A selector lists each property value once over every instance of a class
code:
class Order(region):
    this.region = region
Order("north")
Order("south")
Order("north")
regions = Order.distinct(order -> order.region)
Order("east")
regions

description: Distinct values are compared without conversion and null matches undefined
code:
values = [1, "1", true, 1, null, "1"]
values.push(values[99])
kinds = values.distinct()
[kinds.length, values.length, kinds]

description: Records with the same contents are one value while instances stay apart
code:
class Robot(name):
    this.name = name
ada = Robot("ada")
twin = Robot("ada")
spots = [{x: 1, y: 2}, {y: 2, x: 1}, {x: 2, y: 1}]
[spots.distinct().length, [ada, twin, ada].distinct().length]

description: A class-level rule keeps the distinct regions of each customer
code:
class Customer(name):
    this.name = name
class Order(customer, region):
    this.customer = customer
    this.region = region
$Customer.regions = Order.filter(order -> order.customer == $Customer).distinct(order -> order.region)
ada = Customer("ada")
Order(ada, "north")
Order(ada, "south")
Order(ada, "north")
ada.regions

description: The distinct tags of every post stay live as posts and tags change
code:
class Post(tags):
    this.tags = tags
first = Post(["rust", "logic"])
Post(["logic", "go"])
inuse = Post.flatMap(post -> post.tags).distinct()
first.tags.push("go")
Post(["sql"])
inuse

description: Every NaN is kept because NaN matches no value
A distinct selector that is not a function raises a TypeError
code:
failure = ""
try:
    [1, 2].distinct(5)
catch error:
    failure = error
failure

description: Predicate counts keep each team's open jobs and matching list items live
code:
class Team(name): this.name = name
class Job(team, done):
    this.team = team
    this.done = done
$Team.open = Job.count(job -> job.team == $Team and not job.done)
team = Team("north")
first = Job(team, false)
Job(team, true)
values = [1, 4, 7]
large = values.count(value -> value > 3)
assert(team.open, 1)
first.done = true
values.push(9)
[team.open, large]

description: A list's mode follows pushes and keeps the first of tied items
code:
sizes = ["M", "S", "M", "L"]
top = sizes.mode()
sizes.push("L")
assert(top, "M")
sizes.push("L")
top

description: A selector finds the most common property value over every instance of a class
code:
class Order(size):
    this.size = size
Order("M")
Order("L")
Order("L")
popular = Order.mode(order -> order.size)
Order("M")
Order("M")
popular

description: Mode counts null and undefined as one value and every NaN on its own
code:
values = [0 / 0, 0 / 0, 1, null]
values.push(values[99])
top = values.mode()
readings = [0 / 0, 0 / 0, 1]
[top, String(readings.mode()), String(1 / [-0, 0, 1].mode())]

description: A class-level rule keeps the favorite choice of each team
code:
class Team(name):
    this.name = name
class Vote(team, choice):
    this.team = team
    this.choice = choice
$Team.favorite = Vote.filter(vote -> vote.team == $Team).mode(vote -> vote.choice)
red = Team("red")
Vote(red, "tea")
swing = Vote(red, "coffee")
Vote(red, "coffee")
swing.choice = "tea"
red.favorite

description: A mode selector that is not a function raises a TypeError
code:
failure = ""
try:

catch error:
    failure = error
failure

description: A noun query reads the most frequent item of a list with mode of
code:
list = [3, 4, 4]
num = mode of list
list.push(3)
list.push(3)
num

description: Noun queries total and bound a population as instances are created
code:
class Order(amount):
    this.amount = amount
Order(20)
Order(45)
revenue = sum of Order.map(order -> order.amount)
largest = max of Order.map(order -> order.amount)
Order(80)
[revenue, largest]

description: A class-level rule keeps each object's fill color with mode of
code:
class Obj(parts): this.parts = parts
$Obj.fill_color = mode of $Obj.parts
obj = Obj([2, 5, 5])
obj.parts.push(2)
obj.parts.push(2)
obj.fill_color

description: A noun query takes its operand's postfix chain while binary operators end it
code:
xs = [1, 2, 3]
[sum of xs + 1, sum of xs.map(x -> x * 10), (sum of xs) ** 2, min of xs]

description: A loop variable named like a noun query keeps naming the loop variable
code:
class Item(size): this.size = size
Item(4)
Item(6)
sizes = []
for mode of Item:
    sizes.push(mode.size)
[sizes, max of sizes]
